title: Conormal exterior sections as scalar extension of the algebraic ideal exterior
statement: Let $i:Z\to Y$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-closed-immersion], $U$ an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $V=i^{-1}U$, $A=\Gamma(Y,U)$, $I=(\ker i)(U)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $B=\Gamma(Z,V)$ with its $A$-algebra structure induced by $i$. Put $N=i^*(\ker i)$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and $M=\bigwedge^n_{A/I}(I/I^2)$ regarded as an $A$-module [new-r4-self-tor-conormal-comparison], for any $n\geq0$. There exists a $B$-linear equivalence $e:\bigwedge^n_B N(V)\simeq B\otimes_A M$ [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every tuple $b_j\in\Gamma(U,\ker i)$, it sends the wedge of their canonical pullback-unit images [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] to $1\otimes\mathrm{selfTorIdealWedge}(i,U,n,b)$ [new-t2-self-tor-affine-section]. This is solely a comparison of algebraic modules, without associated sheaves of exterior modules.

source.place: Tag 01R3(2), lemma-affine-conormal; exterior universal property and scalar extension along the quotient-ring identification.

proof.text: The closed immersion gives a surjective A to B with kernel I. Apply affine_conormal_sections with R=A and r=id. Its equivalence takes the cotangent class of selfTorIdealSection(b) to the canonical unit image of b. Since A to B is surjective, scalar lifting makes this equivalence semilinear along the quotient-ring isomorphism q:A/I to B.

The proved private helper exterior_quotient_tensor constructs a B-alternating map on D=N(V) by v to 1 tensor wedge(e inverse(v)). For B-multilinearity, lift a scalar to A and use A-linearity of e inverse, exterior multilinearity over A/I, and tensor balancing. Construct the reverse alternating map on C=I/I squared with values in the B-exterior, using the quotient-ring isomorphism for its A/I-action. Scalar lifting from A to A/I proves its multilinearity. Apply the exterior universal property to both alternating maps.

Extend the reverse exterior map B-linearly to B tensor_A M by b tensor m to b times the image of m. Its composite with the first map is the identity on every pure B-wedge, hence on the whole exterior by linearMap_ext. For the other composite, use tensor extensionality followed by span induction on pure A/I-wedges; lift each scalar in the induction step to A and use tensor balancing. LinearEquiv.ofLinearMap gives the required equivalence. Apply its pure-wedge formula to the unit images and use affine_conormal_sections to identify their inverse images with selfTorIdealSection cotangent classes. Both constructions work in degree zero and over zero rings.

theorem exists_selfTor_conormal_exterior_tensor
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (n : ℕ) (U : Y.affineOpens) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(Y, U.1) Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) := (i.app U.1).hom.toAlgebra
    let N := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj i.ker.toModules
    let M := conormalExteriorModule (Γ(Y, U.1) : Type u) (i.ker.ideal U) n
    ∃ e : (⋀[Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)]^n (N.val.obj (op (i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1))))
        ≃ₗ[Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)] (Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ⊗[Γ(Y, U.1)] M),
      ∀ b : Fin n → i.ker.toModules.val.obj (op U.1),
        e (exteriorPower.ιMulti (Γ(Z, i ⁻¹ᵁ U.1)) n
          (fun j ↦ ((Classical.choose
            (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)).unit.app
              i.ker.toModules).val.app (op U.1) (b j))) =
          1 ⊗ₜ[Γ(Y, U.1)] selfTorIdealWedge i U n b
